evidence.source_reference: Issue #66 (2026-08-03): builder-owned work with one embedded principal decision over-routes to principal ownership

expected_behavior: Altitude routing escalates the decision, not the task: builder-owned work with one embedded principal fork sends that fork up (per the report-the-decision-needed pattern) while the task stays with its builder.
observation: Field report: a task that is overwhelmingly builder-scope but contains one embedded principal-altitude decision gets routed wholesale to principal ownership, inflating ceremony for the whole task instead of escalating the single decision.
reason: Promoted on landed evidence: skills/eng-ladder/SKILL.md Mode 1 states that ownership and consult are distinct outputs and that builder-owned work with one embedded higher-altitude decision stays builder-owned, routed as a required principal consult on the named decision rather than by re-owning the whole item. Escalate-the-decision-not-the-task is shipped behavior, so no further fleet change is owed by this record. Deliberately not claimed: the paired routing positive under-fires in the documented headless shape, which is LADDER-002's measurement question rather than a gap in this lesson.
